translation_en: Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Ali ibn Mudrik, who said: I heard Abu Zurah ibn Amr ibn Jarir narrate from his grandfather Jarir: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said to me during the Farewell Pilgrimage: “Make the people listen.” Then he said: “Do not return to disbelief after me, striking one another's necks.”

Muhammad ibn Ubaydullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah. Ibrahim also said: Salih ibn Kaysan narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There will be trials. The one sitting during them will be better than the one standing, the one standing better than the one walking, and the one walking better than the one rushing toward them. Whoever exposes himself to them will be drawn into them. Whoever finds a refuge or a place of protection should seek it.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There will be trials. The one sitting during them will be better than the one standing, the one standing better than the one walking, and the one walking better than the one rushing toward them. Whoever exposes himself to them will be drawn into them. Whoever finds a refuge or a place of protection should seek it.”

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from an unnamed man, from al-Hasan, who said: I went out with my weapon during the nights of civil strife. Abu Bakrah met me and asked: “Where are you going?” I said: “I want to support the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.” He said: The Messenger of Allah said: “When two Muslims confront one another with their swords, both the killer and the one killed are among the people of the Fire.” It was asked: “This is the killer, but what about the one killed?” He said: “He intended to kill his companion.” Hammad ibn Zayd said: I mentioned this hadith to Ayyub and Yunus ibn Ubayd, hoping they would narrate it to me. They said: Al-Hasan only narrated this from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, from Abu Bakrah. Sulayman narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, with this report. Mual narrated: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us; Ayyub, Yunus, Hisham, and Mual ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from al-Ahnaf, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet. Mamar reported it from Ayyub. Bakkar ibn Abd al-Aziz reported it from his father, from Abu Bakrah. Ghundar said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet. Sufyan did not attribute it to the Prophet when reporting from Mansur.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us; Ibn Jabir narrated to us; Busr ibn Ubaydullah al-Hadrami narrated to me that he heard Abu Idris al-Khawlani, who heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: People used to ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, about good, but I used to ask him about evil for fear it might reach me. I said: “Messenger of Allah, we were in ignorance and evil, then Allah brought us this good. Will there be evil after this good?” He said: “Yes.” I said: “Will there be good after that evil?” He said: “Yes, but it will be tainted.” I asked: “What will taint it?” He said: “People who guide by something other than my guidance; you will recognize some of what they do and disapprove of some.” I asked: “Will there be evil after that good?” He said: “Yes, callers at the gates of Hell. Whoever responds to them, they will throw him into it.” I asked: “Messenger of Allah, describe them to us.” He said: “They will be of our own people and speak our language.” I asked: “What do you command me to do if I live to see that?” He said: “Keep to the community of Muslims and their leader.” I asked: “What if they have no community and no leader?” He said: “Then keep away from all those factions, even if you have to bite the root of a tree, until death comes to you while you are in that state.”

Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us; Haywah and another narrator narrated to us; they said: Abu al-Aswad narrated to us. Al-Layth also reported from Abu al-Aswad, who said: A military expedition was assigned to the people of Medina, and I enlisted in it. I met Ikrimah and told him, and he strongly forbade me to go. Then he said: Ibn Abbas informed me that some Muslims were with the polytheists, swelling the ranks of the polytheists against the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. An arrow would be shot and strike one of them, killing him, or someone would strike and kill him. Then Allah Most High revealed: “Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves...” (Quran 4:97).

Muhammad ibn Kathir informed us; Sufyan informed us; al-Amash narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Wahb. Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told us two reports. I have seen one of them, and I await the other. He told us: “Trustworthiness descended into the depths of people's hearts. Then they learned from the Quran, then they learned from the Sunnah.” He also told us about its removal: “A man will sleep, and trustworthiness will be taken from his heart, leaving a faint trace like a mark. Then he will sleep again, and it will be taken away, leaving a blister-like trace, like an ember you roll over your foot that raises a blister, which you see swollen but empty inside. Then people will begin trading, and hardly anyone will fulfill a trust. It will be said: ‘In such-and-such a tribe there is a trustworthy man.’ A man will be called intelligent, refined, and strong, though his heart contains not even a mustard seed of faith. There was a time when I did not care whom I traded with: if he was Muslim, his Islam would make him return what was due to me; if he was Christian, his authority would make him return it to me. But today I would trade only with so-and-so and so-and-so.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Hatim narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa, who said: He entered upon al-Hajjaj, who said: “Ibn al-Akwa, have you turned back on your heels and become a Bedouin?” He said: “No, but the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, gave me permission to live in the desert.” Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd also said: When Uthman ibn Affan was killed, Salamah ibn al-Akwa went to al-Rabadha, married a woman there, and had children with her. He remained there until a few nights before he died, then he came to Medina.

Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us; Malik informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Sasaa, from his father, from Abu Said al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The time is near when the best property a Muslim can have will be sheep, which he follows to the mountain peaks and places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from trials.”

Muadh ibn Fadalah narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The people questioned the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, so persistently that they distressed him. One day he ascended the pulpit and said: “You will not ask me about anything without my explaining it to you.” I looked to my right and left and saw every man with his head wrapped in his garment, weeping. A man stood who, when he quarreled, was attributed to someone other than his father, and said: “Prophet of Allah, who is my father?” He replied: “Your father is Hudhafah.” Then Umar stood and said: “We are pleased with Allah as our Lord, Islam as our religion, and Muhammad as our Messenger. We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials.” The Prophet said: “I have never seen good and evil like I have today. Paradise and the Fire were shown to me until I saw them beyond this wall.” Qatadah said: This hadith is mentioned in connection with the verse: “O you who believe, do not ask about things which, if made clear to you, would distress you” (Quran 5:101).

Abbas al-Narsi said: Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us; Said narrated to us; Qatadah narrated to us, that Anas told them this report from the Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. He said: Each man had wrapped his head in his garment and was weeping. He said: “Seeking refuge in Allah from the evil of trials,” or “I seek refuge in Allah from the evil of trials.”

Khalifah said to me: Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us; Said and Mutamir narrated to us, from their father, from Qatadah, that Anas told them this report from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “Seeking refuge in Allah from the evil of trials.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me; Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Mamar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: He stood beside the pulpit and said: “The trial is here, the trial is here, from where the horn of Satan rises”—or he said, “the horn of the sun.”

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us; Layth narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was facing east, say: “Beware, the trial is here, from where the horn of Satan rises.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Azhar ibn Sad narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “O Allah, bless our Syria; O Allah, bless our Yemen.” They said: “And our Najd?” He said: “O Allah, bless our Syria; O Allah, bless our Yemen.” They said: “Messenger of Allah, and our Najd?” I think he said the third time: “There will be earthquakes and trials there, and from there the horn of Satan will rise.”

Ishaq al-Wasiti narrated to us; Khalid narrated to us, from Bayan, from Wabarah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Said ibn Jubayr, who said: Abdullah ibn Umar came out to us, and we hoped he would tell us a good hadith. A man hurried to him and said: “Abu Abd al-Rahman, tell us about fighting during times of trial, for Allah says, ‘Fight them until there is no more trial’ (Quran 2:193).” He said: “Do you know what that trial was? May your mother grieve for you! Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, fought the polytheists, and entering their religion was the trial. That is not like your fighting for kingship.”

Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us; my father narrated to us; al-Amash narrated to us; Shaqiq narrated to us: I heard Hudhayfah say: While we were sitting with Umar, he asked: “Which of you remembers what the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said about trials?” He said: “A man's trial in his family, wealth, children, and neighbor is expiated by prayer, charity, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong.” Umar said: “I am not asking you about that, but about the trial that surges like the waves of the sea.” He said: “You need not fear it, Commander of the Faithful; there is a closed door between you and it.” Umar asked: “Will the door be broken or opened?” He said: “It will be broken.” Umar said: “Then it will never be closed again.” I said: “Yes.” We asked Hudhayfah: “Did Umar know what the door was?” He said: “Yes, as surely as I know that a night comes before tomorrow. I told him a report that was not muddled.” We were reluctant to ask him who the door was, so we asked Masruq to ask. He said: “Who is the door?” He replied: “Umar.”

Said ibn Abi Maryam informed us; Muhammad ibn Jafar informed us, from Sharik ibn Abdullah, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Musa al-Ashari, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, went out to one of the gardens of Medina to relieve himself, and I followed him. When he entered the garden, I sat by its gate and said to myself: “Today I will be the Prophet's gatekeeper,” although he had not ordered me to do so. The Prophet went and relieved himself, then sat on the rim of a well, uncovered his shins, and lowered his legs into it. Abu Bakr came asking permission to enter. I said: “Wait here until I ask permission for you.” He waited. I went to the Prophet and said: “Prophet of Allah, Abu Bakr asks permission to enter.” He said: “Let him in, and give him the good news of Paradise.” Abu Bakr entered and sat to the Prophet's right, uncovered his shins, and lowered his legs into the well. Then Umar came. I said: “Wait here until I ask permission for you.” The Prophet said: “Let him in, and give him the good news of Paradise.” Umar came and sat to the Prophet's left, uncovered his shins, and lowered his legs into the well. The rim became full, leaving no room. Then Uthman came. I said: “Wait here until I ask permission for you.” The Prophet said: “Let him in, and give him the good news of Paradise, along with a trial that will befall him.” Uthman entered and found no space with them, so he moved to the opposite edge of the well, uncovered his shins, and lowered his legs into it. I began wishing for a brother of mine and praying to Allah that he would come. Said ibn al-Musayyab said: I interpreted this as their graves being together there, while Uthman was apart.

Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Jafar informed us, from Shu'bah, from Sulayman, who said: I heard Abu Wail say: Usamah was asked: “Will you not speak to this man?” He said: “I have spoken to him privately, without opening a door that would make me the first to open it. I am not going to tell a man, after he has become ruler over two people, ‘You are better,’ after hearing the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘A man will be brought and thrown into the Fire, where he will go round and round like a donkey turning a millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say: “So-and-so, did you not command what is right and forbid what is wrong?” He will say: “I used to command what is right but not do it, and forbid what is wrong but do it.”’”

Uthman ibn al-Haytham narrated to us; Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Bakrah, who said: Allah benefited me with a statement during the Battle of the Camel. When news reached the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that the Persians had made the daughter of Kisra their ruler, he said: “A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never succeed.”

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us; Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us; Abu Husayn narrated to us; Abu Maryam Abdullah ibn Ziyad al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: When Talhah, al-Zubayr, and Aishah set out for Basra, Ali sent Ammar ibn Yasir and al-Hasan ibn Ali. They came to Kufa and ascended the pulpit. Al-Hasan stood at the top of the pulpit, and Ammar stood below him. We gathered around them and heard Ammar say: “Aishah has set out for Basra. By Allah, she is the wife of your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in this world and the Hereafter. But Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is testing you to see whether you obey Him or her.”

Abu Nuaim narrated to us; Ibn Abi Ghaniyyah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Abu Wail: Ammar stood on the pulpit in Kufa, mentioned Aishah and her journey, and said: “She is the wife of your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in this world and the Hereafter, but she is part of the trial you are facing.”

Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us; Amr informed me: I heard Abu Wail say: Abu Musa and Abu Masud visited Ammar when Ali had sent him to the people of Kufa to urge them to join him. They said: “Since you accepted Islam, we have never seen you do anything we disliked more than your haste in this matter.” Ammar said: “Since you both accepted Islam, I have never seen you do anything I disliked more than your delay in this matter.” He gave each of them a robe, then they went to the mosque.

Abdan narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah, from al-Amash, from Shaqiq ibn Salamah, who said: I was sitting with Abu Masud, Abu Musa, and Ammar. Abu Masud said: “Of all your companions, I could criticize anyone except you. Since you accompanied the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, I have seen nothing in you more objectionable than your haste in this matter.” Ammar said: “Abu Masud, since you and your companion accompanied the Prophet, I have seen nothing in either of you more objectionable than your delay in this matter.” Abu Masud was wealthy, and he said: “Boy, bring two robes.” He gave one to Abu Musa and the other to Ammar, saying: “Wear them to Friday prayer.”

Abdullah ibn Uthman narrated to us; Abdullah informed us; Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri. Hamzah ibn Abdullah ibn Umar informed me that he heard Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “When Allah sends down punishment upon a people, it strikes everyone among them; then they will be resurrected according to their deeds.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us; Israil Abu Musa narrated to us. I met him in Kufa when he came to Ibn Shubrumah and said: “Take me to Isa so I may admonish him.” Ibn Shubrumah seemed to fear for him and did not do so. Al-Hasan narrated to us: When al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both, marched with troops toward Muawiyah, Amr ibn al-As said to Muawiyah: “I see a battalion that will not turn back until its last ranks have turned.” Muawiyah said: “Who will protect the families of the Muslims?” He said: “I will.” Abdullah ibn Amir and Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah said: “Let us meet him and offer him a settlement.” Al-Hasan said: I heard Abu Bakrah say: While the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was giving a sermon, al-Hasan came. The Prophet said: “This son of mine is a leader, and perhaps Allah will use him to reconcile two factions of the Muslims.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us. Amr said: Muhammad ibn Ali informed me that Harmalah, the freedman of Usamah, informed him. Amr said: I saw Harmalah. He said: Usamah sent me to Ali and told me: “He will ask you now, ‘What kept your companion away?’ Tell him: ‘He says: If you were in a lion's jaws, I would love to be there with you. But this is a matter I have not seen clearly.’” Ali gave me nothing, so I went to al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and Ibn Jafar, and they loaded my mount with provisions.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi, who said: When the people of Medina deposed Yazid ibn Muawiyah, Ibn Umar gathered his family and children and said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “A banner will be raised on the Day of Resurrection for every betrayer.” We pledged allegiance to this man under the pledge to Allah and His Messenger. I know of no greater betrayal than for a man to be given the pledge to Allah and His Messenger, then to be fought. I do not know anyone among you who has deposed him or pledged allegiance in this matter without that becoming the decisive point between me and him.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Abu Shihab narrated to us, from Awf, from Abu al-Minhal, who said: When Ibn Ziyad and Marwan were in Syria, Ibn al-Zubayr rose up in Mecca, and the Quran reciters rose up in Basra, I went with my father to Abu Barzah al-Aslami. We entered his home and found him sitting in the shade of a small upper room made of reeds. We sat with him, and my father asked him for a hadith, saying: “Abu Barzah, do you see what has happened among the people?” The first thing he said was: “I hope for reward from Allah for having awakened displeased with the living members of Quraysh. Arabs, you were in the state you know: humiliation, few in number, and misguidance. Allah saved you through Islam and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, until you reached the position you see. This worldly life is what has corrupted relations among you. By Allah, that man in Syria is fighting only for worldly gain; these people among you are fighting only for worldly gain; and that man in Mecca is fighting only for worldly gain.”

Adam ibn Abi Iyas narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Wasil al-Ahdab, from Abu Wail, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said: The hypocrites today are worse than they were in the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. In those days they concealed their hypocrisy; today they make it public.
